title: The Trail of the Sepik Basin
premise: Cyrus Sterling, a salvage diver haunted by the disappearance of her brother on a classified navy operation, recovers a sealed chest from a wreck in the Sepik Basin stamped with the seal of a nation that no longer exists. The chest contains evidence of an illegal expedition — and a living passenger everyone believed dead. Blackmailed by a disgraced naval intelligence officer into joining a cover-up expedition upriver, Cyrus must decide between protecting the found family she's built among the salvage crew and exposing a truth that could destroy them all. In the end, she chooses justice outside the law: she delivers the evidence to the victim's family rather than to any government, burns her own salvage claim, and finally stops measuring life in miles.
about_author: Juniper Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime archaeologist who spent a decade documenting river wrecks across Southeast Asia and Melanesia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who find family in the unlikeliest places, drawing on real expeditions she can never fully talk about.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Cyrus Sterling's POV. Three years after her brother's disappearance, Cyrus dives a navy-restricted wreck off the Sepik delta, measuring her life in nautical miles. Her salvage crew — gruff engineer Bo, young deckhand Nia, and cook-turned-navigator Salim — are the only family she has left. Emotional beat: grief worn as routine, the ache beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Chest with No Country
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. On the final dive, the river gives up a lead-lined chest stamped with the seal of Vaskaria, a nation dissolved decades ago. Inside: expedition logs, photographs of her brother alive, and coordinates deep in the Sepik Basin. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: Visitors at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. A naval intelligence officer, Commander Ilse Rennick, arrives asking questions about 'recovered materials.' Bo lies badly and knows it. The crew realizes the chest has painted a target on their boat. Emotional beat: protective fear, loyalty tested by helplessness.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Rennick offers a deal: join a sanctioned 'survey' expedition upriver or face charges that will sink the crew. She reveals fragments — the chest came from an expedition declared lost, one that included Cyrus's brother. Emotional beat: rage and calculation; the trap dressed as a lifeline.

chapters.title: Provisions and Lies
chapters.summary: Salim's POV. The crew provisions the boat for a journey none of them believe in. Salim quietly copies the chest's documents before Rennick's people seal them away, hiding duplicates in his spice tins. Emotional beat: quiet defiance; love expressed as preparation.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The expedition pushes into the Sepik Basin — crocodile water, mist, villages watching from stilts. Nia, youngest aboard, maps the river's moods and notices they're being shadowed by another boat. Emotional beat: wonder braided with dread; adolescence ending early.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At a riverside village, an elder recognizes the Vaskarian seal and tells of outsiders who came years ago and never left — men taken into the interior. One name matches her brother's. Emotional beat: hope arriving as something almost unbearable.

chapters.title: What Rennick Knows
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Alone in her cabin, Rennick reviews her true orders: recover the chest's contents, confirm no survivors, and bury the expedition's crimes — including what was done to the taken men. Emotional beat: a careerist confronting the shape of her complicity.

chapters.title: The Shadow Boat
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The second boat closes in at night; it's crewed by private contractors, not navy — someone else wants the chest. A tense standoff ends without shots but leaves the crew certain they're expendable. Emotional beat: solidarity forged under threat.

chapters.title: Into the Interior
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following the logbook coordinates overland with a village guide, the party finds the expedition's abandoned camp — and fresh graves, some recent. Cyrus finds her brother's knife. Emotional beat: mourning and fury entwined; the dead leaving instructions.

chapters.title: The Man Who Didn't Drown
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Deep in the basin, they find him: Tomas Sterling, alive, half-feral, kept hidden by villagers for three years because he is the sole witness to the expedition's massacre of local laborers. Emotional beat: joy collapsing into horror — reunion as wound.

chapters.title: Testimony in the Dark
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. By firelight, Tomas recounts the truth: the Vaskarian expedition trafficked artifacts and people, and when he tried to stop it, they left him for dead. Every institution meant to deliver justice is implicated. Emotional beat: the weight of surviving to testify.

chapters.title: Rennick's Choice
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Ordered to eliminate witnesses, Rennick stalls, then secretly warns Cyrus — not out of conscience alone, but because her own brother died on that same expedition. Emotional beat: two griefs recognizing each other across enemy lines.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The contractors ambush the group at the river confluence. Salim is shot covering the others' escape; the duplicate documents scatter into the current. Nia saves what she can. Emotional beat: first blood, first irreparable loss.

chapters.title: Salim's Tins
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Grieving, Bo discovers Salim hid a second set of duplicates inside the boat's hull — the old man planned for betrayal before it ever came. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the dead still protecting the living.

chapters.title: The Long Paddle Down
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Fleeing downriver by canoe with Tomas and the evidence, pursued by both contractors and now Rennick's own command, the crew becomes a fugitive family. Emotional beat: exhaustion, trust, the strange peace of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Cornered by her superiors, Rennick chooses sides: she feeds the contractors false coordinates and gives Cyrus the location of the one journalist who broke the original story years ago — then surrenders herself to buy time. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: The Chest Returns to the River
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Trapped at the delta, Cyrus makes her stand: she scuttles the original chest into deep water where no government can claim it, keeping only the testimony. The contractors' boat grounds on the wreck she knows better than anyone. Emotional beat: the diver choosing what the river keeps.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Rather than hand evidence to authorities, Cyrus and Tomas deliver the testimony to the families of the massacred laborers and the journalist, letting the victims' community decide its use. Emotional beat: justice as gift, not verdict; power returned to the wronged.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Anchor
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Weeks later, the story breaks worldwide. Rennick faces trial; the crew's names are cleared. Nia, changed, takes the helm for the first time. Emotional beat: the young inheriting the wheel; grief settling into memory.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus dives one last time — not for salvage, but to say goodbye to the wreck, the chest, and the version of herself who measured life in miles. She surfaces lighter. Emotional beat: release; mourning completed, not escaped.

chapters.title: Home Water
chapters.summary: Full crew POV, braided. With Tomas aboard and Salim's empty chair honored at the table, the boat heads upriver toward the village that sheltered him — carrying supplies, medicine, and no secrets. Emotional beat: found family made whole; the journey home as beginning, not end.
